 Notes from the Editors
 Ponatinib–Blinatumomab for Ph-Positive ALL 
 The pace of change in the treatment of cancer is extraordinary. It wasn’t that long ago when the introduction of the first clinical tyrosine kinase inhibitor, imatinib, revolutionized the treatment of Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-positive ALL) when used in combination with chemotherapy. But with further advances in biologic therapies, do we still need chemotherapy?
In this issue of the Journal , Chiaretti et al. ask that question by comparing what we would now consider the traditional treatment, imatinib plus chemotherapy, with the use of a third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor, ponatinib, combined with a bispecific T-cell–engaging antibody, blinatumomab, that induces immune-mediated lysis of tumor cells. And the answer? Well, you’ll have to read the paper. But I’ll tell you that, in the future, we may have excellent alternatives to chemotherapy for the treatment of Ph-positive ALL.
Eric
 Eric J. Rubin, M.D., Ph.D.
